newsitem.title: MOROCCO: S Korea's Daewoo to buy Morocco's Hyatt Regency. [CORRECTED 20:45 GMT]
newsitem.headline: S Korea's Daewoo to buy Morocco's Hyatt Regency. [CORRECTED 20:45 GMT]

text.p: South Korean giant Daewoo Corp is expected to buy the five-star Hyatt Regency hotel located in Rabat, a Moroccan government official said on Friday.
(Corrects to show that Daewoo has not confirmed purchase).

The conglomerate plans to purchase the luxurious hotel, located in a residential area close to the Rabat Royal palace, for 18 billion dirhams ($21 million), a privatisation ministry official told Reuters.

Daewoo was continuing talks with the Moroccan authorities on implementing a $500 million investment projects deal in the North African country comprising telecommunications, tourism and electronics, officials said.
Daewoo signed an investment agreement with the government last July in Rabat.
A Daewoo representative in Rabat confirmed the purchase plan but declined to comment.
The initial offer for the hotel sale was set at 25 billion dirhams but reduced finally to 18 billion dirhams, a market analyst said.
"The move aimed at attracting a professional international investor and develop high standards of tourism accommodations from which the country will benefit on the long term," the analyst said.
Established in 1988, the Hyatt Regency hotel has 220 rooms, 28 suites and employs a staff of more 300.
